display_name: Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur vs. Mahmud Lodi
one_line: The Mughal founder Babur and Afghan rival Mahmud Lodi clash over the Ghaghra-Ganges in 1529, as rival claimants to north India’s future.

appearance.age_look: early 40s for Babur (lean, battle-hardened), late 30s for Mahmud Lodi (broad-shouldered and vigorous)
appearance.face: Babur has an oval face, fair-olive Central Asian complexion, sharp nose, trimmed mustache and short pointed beard with thoughtful, slightly tired eyes; Mahmud Lodi has a square jaw, medium-brown Afghan complexion, thicker brows, straight nose, neatly trimmed mustache and beard, with an intense, determined gaze; default expressions are Babur calm and assessing, Mahmud grimly resolute.
appearance.hair: Babur’s black hair is mostly hidden under a high, slightly conical Central Asian turban cap wrapped in deep green cloth with a thin gold band; Mahmud Lodi’s black hair is tied back under a tall, white Afghan-style turban wound tightly with a subtle grey stripe.
appearance.costume: Babur wears an era-accurate Mughal-Central Asian outfit: a long quilted cotton jama (robe) in muted warm red with fine vertical stitching and a wrap closure to the right, reaching mid-calf, worn over a dark teal under-tunic and narrow cream churidar trousers; his jama has a thin patterned border in gold and dark green along the front edge and cuffs, and he wears a wide brown leather belt with a simple metal buckle, soft dark-brown leather boots reaching mid-calf, and a plain steel bracer on his left wrist; Mahmud Lodi wears a north Indian-Afghan commander’s garb: a knee-length, sleeveless coat-of-plates over a long-sleeved indigo cotton tunic, the armour made of small riveted steel plates covered in dark brown leather with visible rows of rivets, over loose off-white trousers and soft brown leather boots; he has a dark-blue waist sash, a simple leather belt holding his scabbard, and a modest silver armlet on his right arm; both are fully and modestly clothed in era-appropriate garments, with no exposed torso.
appearance.signature: Babur’s signature prop is a slightly curved steel tulwar with a simple cross-hilt and disc pommel in a plain brown leather scabbard, while Mahmud Lodi’s signature weapon is a straight-bladed Afghan-style sword with a leather-wrapped hilt and iron crossguard, also sheathed at his side.

ref_desc: Babur is a lean, fair-olive man in a muted warm-red quilted jama, deep-green turban cap, dark-teal under-tunic, cream churidar and brown boots with a plain tulwar, facing Mahmud Lodi, a medium-brown, broad-shouldered Afghan in indigo tunic, brown leather-plated coat, white Afghan turban and off-white trousers with an Afghan sword, all in earthy reds, greens, indigo and browns.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two historical rivals from 1529 at the Ghaghra-Ganges: Babur, a lean, fair-olive Central Asian ruler in his early 40s with an oval face, sharp nose, trimmed mustache and small pointed beard, calm assessing eyes, wearing a high, slightly conical Central Asian cap wrapped in deep green cloth with a thin gold band, a muted warm-red quilted cotton jama with fine vertical stitching and a right-side wrap closure reaching mid-calf, a dark-teal under-tunic, cream churidar trousers, a wide brown leather belt, a simple steel bracer on his left wrist, and soft dark-brown mid-calf leather boots; at his side hangs his signature slightly curved steel tulwar in a plain brown leather scabbard. Opposite him, show Mahmud Lodi, late 30s, medium-brown Afghan complexion, square jaw, strong brows, straight nose, neatly trimmed mustache and beard, intense determined eyes, wearing a tall white Afghan-style turban with a subtle grey stripe, a long-sleeved indigo cotton tunic, over it a knee-length sleeveless coat-of-plates made of small steel plates covered in dark brown leather with visible rivet rows, loose off-white trousers, soft brown leather boots, a dark-blue waist sash, a plain leather belt, a modest silver armlet on his right arm, and his straight Afghan sword sheathed at his left hip; keep both figures fully and modestly clothed in historically plausible 16th-century north Indian-Central Asian garments, with earthy dominant colours of muted warm red, deep green, dark teal, indigo, off-white and brown leather, all rendered in a consistent shonen-anime style suitable for repeated redrawing.
